json.title: Infra: move the ETL schemas (62 GB of 133 GB) off the primary, and size the primary to the remaining hot set
json.body:
## Context

Measured on production (11–19 Sep 2026): the primary is a burstable **db.t4g.large** (2 vCPU, 8 GB, $122/month) sitting at **0 CPU credit balance all week**, with 15 h/week above 70% CPU, and the slow requests come in **incidents**, not spread evenly — a tiny org (Udgam, ~1.1 k subjects) suffered 520–700 s requests as collateral damage while another org ran 22 concurrent assignment searches. The database was saturated; whose query it was mattered less than that it was running.

The code fixes (#1067, #1068, #1069, avniproject/avni-client#2096, avniproject/avni-client#2099, #1057) remove an estimated **40–50% of primary database time**, rising to ~55% with #1057. Two infrastructure items remain, and they should be decided **after** those land, because the required size depends on the hot set that is left.

## 1. Move the ETL schemas off the primary

The primary holds **133 GB, of which the ETL schemas are 62 GB**. They compete with the transactional hot set for the same shared buffers and the same IOPS. Metabase reads the ETL schemas, not the tables the code fixes touch — measured: replica-vs-primary for the same reporting query is within 25% (contention is not the constraint) while cold-vs-warm is **20–60×** (cache residency is). Moving the ETL schemas to their own instance frees cache for the transactional workload and is the main lever for reporting latency.

## 2. Size the instance to the hot set

The saving from the code fixes is **not** a smaller instance — it is **avoiding the upgrade** the current trajectory demands. Options priced (ap-south-1, on-demand): db.t4g.xlarge **$244/mo**, db.m7g.large **$175/mo**, db.r7g.large **$199/mo**, against today's **$122/mo**. Staying on db.t4g.large avoids **$53–122/month**. A non-burstable class also removes the credit-exhaustion cliff, which is the mechanism behind the incident pattern.

## To decide

- [ ] Whether the ETL schemas move to a separate instance, and when.
- [ ] Whether the primary moves to a non-burstable class now or after the code fixes are measured in production.
- [ ] Re-measure CPU credits, ReadIOPS and DiskQueueDepth after each code fix reaches production, so the sizing decision uses post-fix numbers.

**Dropped after measurement:** a dedicated database for outlier orgs (apfodisha) — partitioning plus the index plus the client change handles it inside the shared database (1,005 s in the best 4-user run, with three other orgs syncing). Also dropped: per-tenant read replicas (operationally heavy, read-only benefit) and ETL tables for search (staleness).

Evidence: `finalreco.md` §"Cost" and recommendations 9–10.

---
